newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN refugee agency driver killed in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: UN refugee agency driver killed in Rwanda.

text.p: A Rwandan Hutu driver working for the U.N. refugee agency, his wife and two children were killed in Rwanda's troubled northwestern Ruhengeri region, the third attack against aid staff there in just over a week, the UNHCR said on Friday.
Agency spokesman Fernando del Mundo told a briefing that UNHCR had suspended its work in Ruhengeri after the killings and was evacuating its local staff.

Del Mundo said UNHCR was still seeking more details on the circumstances surrounding the killing of the driver Felicien Bucyekabili and family members in Kigombe village on Thursday evening. He said an investigation had been launched.

Kigombe, about eight km (five miles) from Ruhengeri town, was the scene of the murder of a Rwandan Hutu field officer working for the U.N. food agency found dead in his home with his wife, small child and a relative last week. On Tuesday, the body of another Hutu employee of the World Food Programme was found dumped in a forest near Ruhengeri.

Aid officials said the latest killings coincided with a big operation by Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army in Ruhengeri, a predominantly Hutu region near the border with Zaire. "It's almost getting to the stage of pitched battles," one said.

Because of worsening insecurity, Del Mundo said UNHCR expatriate staff had not visited Ruhengeri, which absorbed some 300,000 recent Hutu returnees from Zaire since late last year, for the past two weeks. The region has become a no-go area for many other international agencies including human rights observers.
